claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Thoughtworks Technology Radar volume 34 warns that AI generates increasingly larger amounts of code, causing accumulating cognitive debt and a wider gap between humans and software systems.
claims.quote: The report notably warns of accumulating cognitive debt as AI generates increasingly larger amounts of code and, in so doing, introduces a wider gap between humans and software systems.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The source frames a paradox: agentic systems make code creation quicker, but established practices for discipline and rigor are more vital than ever.
claims.quote: The takeaway for technologists and business leaders is a striking paradox; as agentic systems make it easier to create code quickly, traditional and established practices that ensure discipline and rigor are more vital than ever.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The report says teams are beginning to iterate on coding-agent harnesses with feedforward controls such as Agent Skills and spec-driven development, plus feedback controls such as mutation testing.
claims.quote: Teams are beginning to iterate on coding agent harnesses. These include feedforward controls like Agent Skills and spec-driven development, as well as feedback controls like mutation testing, which trigger self-correction before human review.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source states that as coding agents become more powerful, humans are dangerously tempted to step out of the loop, and teams are beginning to iterate on coding-agent harnesses.
claims.quote: As coding agents become more powerful, humans are dangerously tempted to step out of the loop. Teams are beginning to iterate on coding agent harnesses.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The report says permission-hungry agents create a core tension by seeking maximum access to private data and external systems, making zero trust, sandboxed execution, and defense in depth non-negotiable.
claims.quote: The permission-hungry agents are most useful because they seek the maximum access to private data and external systems, creating a core tension. Zero trust architectures, sandboxed execution, and defense in depth are now non-negotiable table stakes.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The source says AI speed is driving a return to zero trust architecture, DORA metrics, and testability, including managing cognitive debt so developers still understand the systems they build.
claims.quote: The speed of AI is driving a return to well-established techniques like zero trust architecture, DORA metrics, and testability to manage complexity. This includes managing cognitive debt to ensure developers still understand the systems they are building.
